dedupe_keys.name: fragility functions for pile supported wharves and piers under storm surge and waves

description: This model provides fragility functions for pile-supported wharves and piers, the typical berthing structures of ports, under hurricane storm surge and wave loading. Georgios Balomenos and Jamie Padgett of Rice University developed it because port risk models existed mainly for earthquakes, not coastal storms. The framework uses Latin hypercube sampling in a Monte Carlo simulation to estimate uncertain vertical and horizontal demands from surge and waves and uncertain capacities for uplift, shear and flexural failure, produces fragility surfaces that give failure probability as a function of wave height and relative surge elevation, and fits stepwise logistic regression to obtain parameterised deck-pile connection fragility functions ready for regional risk assessment. It is applied to four common deck-pile connection types, including full moment connections with dowels inside or outside the compression zone. Coverage: generic wharf and pier structures, usable for current or projected storm conditions including sea level rise. Access: article in the ASCE Journal of Waterway, Port, Coastal, and Ocean Engineering (2017). Licence and cost: publisher copyright, paid. Caveats: analytical capacity models without field damage validation, and only the deck-pile connection failure modes. It supports hazard exposure and resilience analysis of ports under storms. It complements HAZUS port components and the Gioia Tauro seismic wharf fragility model in the catalogue.
